import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
import warnings
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv("./input/en_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/en_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/en_sample_submission_2.csv")

# Ensure 'before' is string type to avoid float/NaN issues
train["before"] = train["before"].astype(str)
test["before"] = test["before"].astype(str)

# Split train set for hold-out validation (stratified by class)
train_train, val = train_test_split(
    train, test_size=0.05, random_state=42, stratify=train["class"]
)

# Build lookup dictionary with top-2 most common after values for each before
before_to_after_candidates = train_train.groupby("before")["after"].apply(
    lambda x: [mc[0] for mc in Counter(x).most_common(2)]
)
before_to_after_train_dict = before_to_after_candidates.to_dict()


# Validation set predictions using two-stage lookup
def predict_two_stage(token, lookup_dict):
    token_str = str(token)
    if token_str in lookup_dict:
        candidates = lookup_dict[token_str]
        # Primary candidate (most frequent)
        if len(candidates) >= 1:
            return candidates[0]
        # Secondary candidate (if primary fails)
        if len(candidates) >= 2:
            return candidates[1]
    # Fallback to original token
    return token_str


val["pred"] = val["before"].apply(
    lambda x: predict_two_stage(x, before_to_after_train_dict)
)

# Compute accuracy on hold-out validation set
val_acc = (val["pred"] == val["after"]).mean()
print(f"Hold-out validation accuracy (two-stage lookup): {val_acc:.6f}")

# Count OOV cases and fallback
oov_count = val["before"].isin(before_to_after_train_dict).sum()
total_count = len(val)
print(f"OOV rate (fallback needed): {1 - oov_count/total_count:.4f}")

# Build final lookup dictionaries from full training set
before_to_after_full = train.groupby("before")["after"].apply(
    lambda x: [mc[0] for mc in Counter(x).most_common(2)]
)
before_to_after_full_dict = before_to_after_full.to_dict()

# Final prediction on test set using two-stage lookup
test["after"] = test["before"].apply(
    lambda x: predict_two_stage(x, before_to_after_full_dict)
)

# Construct the required 'id' column from sentence_id and token_id
test["id"] = test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str)

# Prepare submission
submission = test[["id", "after"]].copy()
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"Submission shape: {submission.shape}")
print(f"Sample predictions:\n{submission.head(10)}")
